oneTimers: A $5,452M pre-tax gain on selling a 51% stake in Altera, which closed September 12, 2025 and deconsolidated Altera from Intel's results; Intel kept a 49% stake now held as an equity investment. The gain sits in interest and other, net and is excluded from non-GAAP results.

A $1,687M mark-to-market loss on the obligation to issue Escrowed Shares — Intel shares held in escrow for the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act Secure Enclave agreement — also inside interest and other, net; excluded from non-GAAP results.
Gains on equity investments, net were a $221M gain, mostly mark-to-market moves on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales; also excluded from non-GAAP results.

Restructuring and other charges were $175M, versus $5,622M a year ago — the year-ago charge was dominated by impairments, which is why Q3 2024 showed a $9,057M operating loss and a $16,639M net loss attributable to Intel.

Intel flags these results as preliminary: the accounting for its U.S. Government transactions is under consultation with SEC staff (delayed by the government shutdown), and if the staff disagrees, Intel may revise Q3 results — materially.
otherDetail: Other income of $3,891M combines a $221M gain on equity investments, net with $3,670M of interest and other, net. That $3,670M holds the $5,452M pre-tax gain on selling 51% of Altera, partly offset by a $1,687M mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares. The $304M tax provision on $4,574M of pre-tax income is a 6.6% effective rate.
pngFooterNote: GAAP profit flattered by a $5.5B Altera sale gain.

segments.name: Client Computing Group
segments.note: PC and client chips; up 5% YoY on higher client demand. Segment operating income was $2,694M, down from $2,937M a year ago.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; down 1% YoY. Segment operating income was $964M, up from $381M a year ago.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $32M of sales to OUTSIDE customers only (Q3 2025 10-Q). Foundry's total segment revenue was $4,235M, but $4,203M of that was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups — counting it here would count the same dollars twice. Foundry lost $2,321M in the quarter.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mobileye (self-driving tech) and smaller businesses, including Altera through September 11, 2025, when it was deconsolidated. Intel reports this group at $993M; it is shown as $969M here, net of $24M of intersegment eliminations not attributable to Foundry, so the parts sum exactly to Intel's $13,653M total. Up 3% YoY.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 27, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Intel's GAAP net income attributable to Intel was $4,063M, but it includes a $5,452M pre-tax gain from selling 51% of Altera, partly offset by a $1,687M mark-to-market loss on shares escrowed for the U.S. government. Strip those out and non-GAAP net income was $1,023M, or $0.23 a share.
takeaways.title: A $4.1B profit built on a one-time sale

takeaways.text: Client Computing revenue rose 5% to $8,535M and earned $2,694M — the PC business is still Intel's profit engine. Data Center and AI slipped 1% to $4,117M, but its operating income more than doubled to $964M from $381M as costs fell.
takeaways.title: PC chips carried the quarter

takeaways.text: Intel Foundry booked $4,235M of revenue but lost $2,321M, and only $32M came from outside customers. Intel also took in $5.7B from the U.S. government plus $5.0B from NVIDIA and $2.0B from SoftBank — but the accounting for the government deal is still under SEC review, so these results could be revised.
takeaways.title: Foundry still loses money — and mostly sells to Intel

verdict: Intel's revenue rose 3% to $13.7B and it reported $4.1B of net income attributable to Intel, but $5.5B of that came from selling a majority stake in Altera — without it, underlying profit was about $1.0B, and Foundry still lost $2.3B.
